plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous ornamental tree covered in clouds of delicate, fragrant blossoms that appear before the leaves emerge. It is planted widely in parks, along rivers, and in temple grounds, where it draws large crowds for flower-viewing festivals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), South Korea, and temperate regions across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry's peak bloom lasts only about a week, a fleeting beauty that has become a symbol of the transience of life in Japanese culture (mono no aware).

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers atop sturdy stems, grown in countless cultivars. Tulips thrive in regions with cold winters followed by mild springs and peak in mid-April in many northern gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, Turkey, Central Asia origins, and gardens throughout North America and Europe
plants.funFact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, a single rare bulb could sell for more than the price of a luxurious canal house.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A native wild daffodil with pale yellow outer petals and a deeper golden trumpet. It carpets woodlands and meadows in early spring, often late-blooming in cooler uplands where April is the peak.
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, Belgium, and Spain; naturalized in parts of North America
plants.funFact: Daffodil bulbs contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that produces dense panicles of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In parts of the Southern Hemisphere and tropics, some trees bloom outside the main season, and in warm northern regions such as parts of Mexico and Southern Asia flowering begins around spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer in Northern Hemisphere subtropics (April to June); October to December in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Mexico, India, Florida, California, and parts of Africa and Australia
plants.funFact: A carpet of fallen jacaranda flowers is said to bring good luck in some places, and in Pretoria, South Africa, the city is known as the 'Jacaranda City'.
